questions.question: An agent retries with only the latest test failure. What typically happens over several attempts?
options: It fixes the latest problem and forgets earlier fixes, so scores oscillate
questions.explanation: Retry went 2 -> 5 -> 4 -> 5 of 7 and never solved it.

questions.question: What does each Reflexion attempt see?
options: The spec plus every reflection written so far in this task
questions.explanation: Accumulated lessons are what made the scores climb 2, 5, 6, 7.

questions.question: Why does evaluate() run candidate code in a separate interpreter with -I and a timeout?
options: Generated code is untrusted; a crash, infinite loop or side effect must not affect the agent's own process
questions.explanation: Never exec generated code in your own process; Phase 10 adds real sandboxes.

questions.question: Where does the verdict in Reflexion come from?
options: The model's opinion of its code
An external evaluator: here, unit tests
questions.explanation: As in Lesson 5, external signal is what makes self-improvement work.

questions.question: A model writes reflections like 'be more careful next time'. What's the likely effect?
options: Little: vague reflections give the next attempt nothing specific to change
questions.explanation: Useful reflections name the failing case and the change.

questions.question: How does Reflexion differ from episodic memory?
options: Reflexion keeps lessons across attempts at one task; episodic memory keeps episodes across many tasks and retrieves the relevant few
